subject: Post-demo: Finarc evidence export — who-accessed fields and delivery format
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@finarc.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Finarc evidence export — who-accessed fields and delivery format

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the few follow-ups we promised: we heard that Finarc needs a WHO-ACCESSED export for audit and SOX/SOC evidence — specifically a row-level export that shows who accessed customer data, what resource they touched, the action, and a UTC timestamp.

To make sure we produce exactly what your compliance team needs, can you confirm the following two items?

1) Required columns: can you confirm you need (a) user_id or user_hash, (b) resource_path, (c) action (read/write/delete), (d) timestamp_utc, (e) user_role, (f) source_ip, and (g) session_id? If there are others (e.g., request_id, model_version) please list them.

2) Delivery & residency: do you want the extract as CSV or JSON/Parquet? Also confirm the retention window we should include in the sample (you mentioned 12 months on the call — do you want a 90-day sample slice for validation?). Finally, confirm data residency constraints (we'll ensure the export is produced from our us-east region if required).

We attached a brief sample schema (redwood-access-export-sample-schema.md) showing header examples and hashing options for PII. If you prefer hashed user identifiers, we can HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-provided salt and include a note about the irreversible hash in the header.

Next steps we propose: once you confirm the column set and delivery mechanism (S3 presigned link vs SFTP), we will produce a 90-day sample extract within 2 business days for you and your audit team to validate.

Thanks — want to loop Ben in on logistics and Rachel for the compliance mapping.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0118

Attachments: redwood-access-export-sample-schema.md (text), finarc-evidence-checklist.pdf (referenced)
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@finarc.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: George Huang <g.huang@finarc.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Finarc evidence export — who-accessed fields and delivery format

Olga — thanks, good summary. Confirming the compliance team's requirements below:

- Required columns: user_id (we prefer not to receive raw PII; hashed_user_id is fine if you include the hash algorithm and salt provenance), resource_path, action (enum: READ, WRITE, DELETE), timestamp_utc (ISO8601), user_role, source_ip, request_id.

- Retention window: full 13 months of history retained, but for initial validation please provide a 90-day sample (we need both the CSV and a JSON lines version to test ingestion).

- Residency: all extracts must be produced from and stored in AWS us-east-1 buckets we control. Presigned link (HTTPS) is acceptable but must be set for a short expiration (24h).

- Redaction: we cannot accept raw user emails or phone numbers in the export. If you hash identifiers, please document the hashing method.

- Delivery SLA for the sample: 3 business days. For production exports we will define a cadence (monthly or ad-hoc) and expect encryption-in-transit.

I attached our internal evidence checklist for SOC review (finarc-evidence-checklist.pdf) — it lists the exact field names the auditors will look for.

One more ask: can you confirm whether IP addresses are stored as full IPv4/IPv6 strings or if you do any truncation/anonymization by default?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Liu
Security & Compliance Manager, Finarc
jane.liu@finarc.com

Attachments: finarc-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Finarc evidence export — who-accessed fields and delivery format

Olga / team — quick internal plan based on Jane's reply:

- Schema: we'll produce both CSV and JSONL sample outputs. Use header fields: hashed_user_id (HMAC-SHA256), resource_path, action, timestamp_utc, user_role, source_ip, request_id, model_version. We'll include a small README that states hashing algorithm and salt handling (salt not shared).

- Residency: engineering can generate the extract from our us-east-1 export job and place it into an S3 temp bucket that will only be accessible via a presigned URL. We'll stamp the object with server-side encryption and remove after 48 hours.

- IP addresses: by default we store full IPs in the access log. For this export we can provide them as-is unless Jane requests truncation. Note: auditors often expect full source_ip for forensic timelines.

- Timeline: Ben and I can turn around a 90-day sample by EOD Wednesday (2027-08-11). Neha, can you validate the schema against the SOC checklist and confirm we meet the field names?

Ben — can you own the S3 packaging and share the presigned link once generated?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Product Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

- We'll document the hashing approach in the README; the mapping is irreversible.
